summary: Unit tests for the fold — determinism plus the per-field merge rules. Two things here are contracts rather than coverage. The determinism test folds the same records forward, reversed and shuffled and compares stableStringify output, which is what pins 'git-union interleave order is irrelevant'; break ts-sort or the canonical-JSON tie-break and this is the test that fails. The alias-cap tests pin the newest-first trim: five writes of six aliases each — every one individually inside the capture prompt's 6-10 guidance — must fold to at most ALIAS_MAX, keeping the newest and dropping the oldest, which is the whole argument that alias bloat is a fold problem and not a writing problem. They also pin the 4-alias floor, so a note whose individual aliases each exceed the word budget can never trim to nothing.
